name: Quanta Services
key_signal: Price has broken below its 50-day moving average (635 vs 704) with negative MACD momentum and RSI under 40, unwinding a chunk of the prior 42% six-month rally even as the stock still trades at 87x trailing earnings.
thesis: Quanta remains a structural beneficiary of grid modernization, data-center power buildout, and electrification capex, evidenced by 26% revenue growth and 51% earnings growth—rare combination for a mega-cap industrial. The stock is still above its 200-day SMA with an intact golden cross, and 26 analysts rate it a consensus 'buy,' suggesting institutional conviction in the long-term secular story remains intact despite the pullback from its $788.75 52-week high.
bear_case: The technical picture has deteriorated meaningfully: price is down 11% over the last month, sitting 10% below its 50-day average with negative MACD histogram and RSI near 39, indicating the momentum that drove the 42% six-month rally has reversed and could continue mean-reverting toward the 200-day SMA near $552 (a further ~13% downside). This is happening while the stock trades at a demanding 87x trailing P/E, 38.6x forward P/E, and 10.5x book value—multiples that leave zero room for error and are highly sensitive to any deceleration in the 26% revenue growth rate or margin compression (operating margin is already thin at 4.2%), especially with elevated leverage (debt/equity ~69) and high beta (1.215) amplifying downside in a risk-off environment for high-multiple industrials.
